problem: C66 found that critical targets mostly lay outside covered dependency-cell joins, leaving CPU work and terrain/service latency unresolved.
implementation: Optional per-task calling-thread CPU endpoints, per-physical-thread CPU unions, separate initially-pending terrain initializer/noninitializer API spans and GPU-service receiver spans. Existing RAII context/bounds/failure/cleanup machinery is reused. Normal hooks compile out; dispatch_job binds the same receiver Result before preserving its original ? propagation. No production scheduling or cache algorithm changes.

design_review.scope: Test-only physical-thread CPU and terrain/service API attribution on accepted C66 production; no held scheduler changes.
design_review.production_diff: TerrainJob and dispatch_job gain cfg(test) scalar-label/span hooks. dispatch_job binds the same receiver result before the original ? propagation, preserving both transport and original worker errors. Ordinary module visibility is unchanged: observer visibility widening is under cfg(test). No production algorithm, ownership, ordering, cache or scheduling change.
design_review.normal_library: Ordinary release builds and nm scan pass; no observer symbols. Normal SHA differs from C66, so no prior byte identity or speedup claimed.
measurement_contract: Task CPU snapshots are taken inside task wall endpoints on the same physical thread, enforced by the existing non-Send task context. Inclusive CPU includes nested tasks and probe work on this thread, excluding service-thread work.

CPU endpoint intervals are unioned per physical thread; missing/reversed readings leave aggregate CPU null while per-worker coverage is retained. Whole-task CPU is not interpolated into partial p95 tails. CPU/wall is not machine utilization.

Terrain cells only start a span on an initially unfinished snapshot. finish classifies actual initializer versus noninitializer and preserves original Result. Ready calls are excluded; initializer spans can include copying/cache/generation/waits and both include result cloning.

GPU reply span begins after successful job send and covers receiver.recv plus error conversion before event recording. It includes possible remaining queue/service/reply latency and preemption, not pure GPU execution. First-request chunk coordinates are captured before the request vector moves.

Terrain/service events use a separate physical-worker buffer from dependency joins. The tested context/bounds/union/tail logic is shared. Nested categories overlap and cannot be summed as wall fractions.

TerrainSpan Drop records unfinished calls as failed abandoned spans. Existing Task/Trace/Root Drop logic retains failure/missing phases and releases every raw event buffer. No planner/world/GPU owner is held by events.
No collector lock spans generation. Initializer/join candidates keep scalar stamps; ready or inactive callers allocate no event. Only bounded samples and aggregate counts persist after root cleanup.
new_tests: CPU missing/reversed endpoints, nested per-thread unions and valid per-task ratios
Actual optional calling-thread clock and real task recording without a speed threshold
Terrain initialized/ready/racing noninitializer and nested reply categories with original errors, separate dependency buffer and root cleanup
Nested root terrain panic retains abandoned failed span and restores outer reply context
limitations: Whole-region timings remain provisional under known host load; quiet acceptance deferred.
Other locks and service internals are not separately measured.
Probe overhead remains inside observer intervals.

validation.shader_readiness: Actual before/after status4 on every measured observer/paired region.

interpretation: Standard-seed longest basalt-pillar tasks have median GPU reply API fractions96.75/98.34% and calling-thread CPU fractions0.95/0.74%; their root evaluations have medians106.81/99.59ms. Reply spans are not pure GPU execution; remaining queue/service latency and preemption are included.
Longest brown-mushroom task CPU/wall medians52.03/63.39%; median terrain fractions0%, but maximum fractions62.08/51.28%. This is mixed region-dependent work, not proof of purely CPU-bound behavior.
Longest large ancient-debris CPU/wall medians86.22/97.29%; median terrain0%, maximum26.23/28.19%. Longest-task wall medians38.88/9.96ms; the second seed has less absolute time to recover.
Custom/direct spring-open longest tasks have median reply fractions97.77/98.09%, with task wall medians25.96/26.29ms. Early patch-fire also has large terrain intervals.
Some other long tasks have low CPU without entering measured terrain or dependency joins. Other locks, preemption and unmeasured paths remain possible. Residual time is unclassified.
Different medians need not sum or describe one representative task. CPU, overlapping API spans and per-worker sums cannot be added as elapsed-time shares.
decision: Select as diagnostic-only evidence, without speedup or no-regression acceptance. User deferred quiet timing confirmation. Normal observer-symbol scan is empty; normal hash differs from C66, so prior byte identity is not claimed. Actual merged rebuild and full corpus must follow merge.

opportunities.risk: Batching/reuse must preserve exact tile guards, material cache isolation, GPU service fairness and concurrent throughput.
opportunities.complexity: Architectural; distinguish queue/service work and inspect exact tile submissions before selecting a change.
opportunities.validation: Demonstrate fewer relevant submissions/transfers or lower service work with complete original/C66 NBT, ordinary region timings and later quiet/concurrent acceptance.

opportunities.opportunity: Reduce CPU work inside expensive exterior target owners
opportunities.expected_gain: Unknown; current longest main brown/ancient tasks use median21.21/30.62ms calling-thread CPU.
opportunities.risk: Prerequisite state, source order and material-dependent RNG cannot be skipped. C61 moved work earlier without a clear gain; C62-C65 queue changes are still held.
opportunities.complexity: High; inspect/profile owner work before another scheduler.
opportunities.validation: Measure reduced actual CPU/work and full-region results; retain exact output, request order and concurrent coverage.
